cards.title: Loss of Human Connection Biggest Threat to Kids, Not AI
cards.body: A pediatrician argues that screens aren't the real problem—lack of meaningful conversation is. Spending more time talking openly with children matters far more than worrying about technology.

cards.title: Make Halloween Magic for Your Kids This Year
cards.body: A parent ditches cynicism to celebrate autumn traditions like pumpkins and Day of the Dead with family. These moments create genuine connection and wonder for children.

cards.title: Why Feeling Like We Belong Matters for Families
cards.body: Connection comes from people, experiences, and traditions—not just a physical place. Psychological research shows belonging deeply impacts child development and family well-being.

cards.title: 10 Truths Teens Want Parents to Know
cards.body: A psychotherapist shares key insights teens wish their parents understood about adolescence. These truths help caregivers better support their children through this critical developmental stage.

cards.title: Is Your College Student Having a Mid-Semester Meltdown?
cards.body: Parents can help struggling college students regain control without fixing problems for them. Five evidence-based strategies empower young adults to manage grades and stress independently.

cards.title: How Parents Contribute to Adult Child Estrangement
cards.body: Parents who recognize their own behavior's role in estrangement can create paths to reconciliation. Understanding and acceptance start with acknowledging one's contribution to the rift.

cards.title: Wonder-Centered Education Begins With Teachers
cards.body: When educators rediscover wonder, schools transform through shared vulnerability and inquiry. Research shows cultivating openness benefits student learning and development.

cards.title: Misophonia at the Holiday Dinner Table
cards.body: Families can make meaningful memories despite misophonia triggers by making thoughtful accommodations. Simple adjustments help loved ones enjoy time together without stress.
